lessons.title: Stack Basics
lessons.concept: Stack is LIFO (Last In, First Out). Operations: push (add), pop (remove top), peek (view top). All O(1). Used for undo, back, function calls, expression evaluation.

lessons.title: Queue Basics
lessons.concept: Queue is FIFO (First In, First Out). Operations: enqueue (rear), dequeue (front), peek. All O(1) with proper impl. Used for BFS, task scheduling.

practice.question: Which allows enqueue and dequeue both O(1)?
practice.explanation: Circular buffer supports O(1) enqueue/dequeue with fixed capacity.

practice.question: A stack follows which discipline?
practice.explanation: Stacks push/pop at the same end: the most recently added element is removed first (LIFO).

practice.question: A queue follows which discipline?
practice.explanation: Elements are enqueued at the rear and dequeued from the front: earliest first (FIFO).

practice.question: Which real-world process is modelled most naturally by a stack?

options.A: Print jobs on a shared printer

practice.explanation: Undo reverts the most recent action first - LIFO. Printer and FCFS service are FIFO queues; scheduling queues are queues too.

practice.question: Pushing 3 items and then popping once removes:
practice.explanation: LIFO: the last item pushed is at the top and is popped first.

practice.question: Evaluating a postfix expression uses which structure?
practice.explanation: Scan left to right: push operands; on an operator pop two operands, compute, push the result. The final stack top is the value.

questions.question: Structure commonly used for managing function calls and local variables?
questions.explanation: Function call stack uses LIFO → stack.

questions.question: Structure for BFS graph traversal?
questions.explanation: BFS uses queue (FIFO) to explore level by level.

questions.question: Which sorting algorithm has best worst-case for large list?
questions.explanation: Merge sort worst-case O(n log n); quick sort worst O(n²).

questions.question: Which data structure is used by recursion's implicit mechanism?
questions.explanation: Function calls are pushed onto the call stack and returned from in reverse order - exactly LIFO behaviour.

questions.question: Which traversal uses a stack explicitly or implicitly?
questions.explanation: Depth-first traversal explores deep first, deferring siblings - stack behaviour (recursion uses the call stack; iterative DFS uses an explicit one).

questions.question: A circular queue mainly solves which problem of a simple array queue?

options.B: Wasting space at the front after repeated dequeue cycles

questions.explanation: In a plain array queue, dequeueing advances the front and leaves unusable gaps even when empty at the back; wrapping indices (mod n) reuses that space.

questions.question: In a standard stack, insertion and deletion both happen at the:
questions.explanation: A stack has one accessible end - the top - where both push and pop operate, which is what makes it LIFO.

questions.question: Which traversal uses an explicit QUEUE?
questions.explanation: Level-order processes nodes level by level with FIFO enqueue/dequeue; DFS traversals use stacks (or recursion).

questions.question: In a two-stack queue, elements are dequeued by:

options.B: Popping the output stack; refill it from the input stack when empty

questions.explanation: In-stack receives enqueues; out-stack serves dequeues. When out-stack empties, all of in-stack is transferred - each element moves twice total: amortised O(1).

questions.question: A priority queue differs from a normal queue because it:

options.B: Removes the highest/lowest priority element first
options.D: Must be implemented as an array

questions.explanation: Priority queues dequeue by key (usually via a heap), not arrival order - O(log n) enqueue/dequeue with O(1) peek of the extreme.
